chunks: 1281 - And Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Ziyād narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said:

"Seven do not shorten the salat (prayer): the tax collector who goes about in his tax collection, the leader who goes about in his governance, the merchant who goes about in his trade from market to market, the shepherd, the Bedouin, the one who seeks places of rainfall and the growth of trees, the man who seeks hunting intending by it the amusement of the world, and the fighter who cuts off the road."

key_terms.الصَّيْدَ: hunting pursued here for worldly amusement
key_terms.الْأَمِيرُ: the ruler or leader moving within his jurisdiction
key_terms.الْجَابِي: the tax collector who travels in the course of his work
key_terms.يَقْطَعُ السَّبِيلَ: blocks the road; engages in banditry

ai.seo_question: Who does not shorten salat (prayer) while traveling according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning travelers whose movement is habitual or tied to ongoing occupations, indicating that they do not perform qasr in salat (prayer). It lists several categories of people whose travel is treated as part of their regular activity, as well as one who travels for sinful purposes such as banditry.
